purpose: Motivated proof-discovery notes. These trails are navigation and research history, never theorem certifications.

moves.name: Reduce by symmetry
moves.description: Replace equivalent finite objects with canonical representatives, preserving exact hypotheses.

moves.name: Replay independently
moves.description: Check a sourced finite object with a distinct implementation and explicit scope.

moves.name: Audit scope
moves.description: Check that a witness or proof establishes exactly the registered mathematical statement.

moves.name: Find the missing certificate
moves.description: Identify the explicit finite object, witness, or proof trace required for an independent check.

trails.question: How do symmetry reductions change what we can actually verify about union-closed families?

nodes.title: A raw census hides relabeling symmetry
nodes.detail: At n = 4 the unfiltered finite mine records 4,958 families; this counts families that may leave ground elements unused. A full-support count is a different quantity.

nodes.title: Compare canonical encodings under permutations
nodes.detail: Canonical encoding identifies ground-set relabeling orbits. A separate closure-pruned descending construction enumerates full-support families without trying every bitmask.

nodes.title: Reproduce the n = 5 full-support orbit count
nodes.detail: The recorded full-support count is 2,747,402 labeled families and 28,960 relabeling orbits; the latter is separately checked using Burnside's lemma. This is known finite mathematics, not a proof of Frankl.

nodes.title: Test canonical augmentation and independent review
nodes.detail: Obtain independent review of both lemmas and their quantified domain; try pruning noncanonical partial states and independently replaying the resulting orbit count. The conjecture remains open.

trails.question: What would turn the existential Hadwiger claim into an independently replayable finite test?

nodes.title: The upstream statement is an existential graph construction
nodes.detail: The audited comparator gives existence claims involving chromatic and Hadwiger-number bounds, not a listed finite adjacency matrix.

nodes.title: No explicit finite graph accompanies the construction
nodes.detail: A second Lean kernel replay does not supply the graph that this repository's finite graph checker would need. The evidence state remains claim under review.

nodes.title: Extract a graph or obtain independent specialist reviews
nodes.detail: For the finite-witness path, supply a finite graph and independently check a coloring lower bound and clique-minor upper bound. Specialist review of the existential proof is a different acceptance path.

trails.question: Can the claimed Sidorenko counterexample be independently tested outside its author Lean tree?

nodes.title: Reconstruct the claimed bipartite pattern H
nodes.detail: The pinned face table yields an incidence graph with 35 vertices and 66 edges, checked by separate edge-count methods. This only checks the encoded pattern.

nodes.title: The finite host G has not been published
nodes.detail: The upstream proof gives an existence argument from a counter-kernel; no concrete host order, adjacency list, or graph6 witness is supplied.

nodes.title: Produce and independently check host G
nodes.detail: Extract an explicit host and compute both homomorphism density and edge density independently against the exact 66-edge inequality. Until then, the finite witness is not replayed.

trails.question: What separates a certified Ramsey lower bound from a new exact value of R(5,5)?

nodes.title: Start from the published interval 43–46
nodes.detail: The audited published bound is 43 ≤ R(5,5) ≤ 46; neither endpoint equality nor a 43-vertex avoiding coloring is established here.

nodes.title: Check 328 published 42-vertex colorings
nodes.detail: A SHA-256-pinned McKay catalog is checked using two different K5 search methods, reproducing R(5,5) ≥ 43. Complements give color-swapped examples, not a completeness argument.

nodes.title: Require a new witness or checked exclusion
nodes.detail: Improving the lower bound needs a K43 coloring with no monochromatic K5; improving the upper bound needs an exhaustive argument with independently checked proof traces. A solver verdict alone is insufficient.
